stories.statLabel: days to carry out Iran's plan
stories.headline: Iran pushes a faster ceasefire plan with the US
body: Iran says its seven-step plan can now be carried out within two days.
It includes quickly reopening the Strait of Hormuz and returning to nuclear talks.
Talks with Qatari mediators continue as the region braces for possible new fighting.
stories.joke: Faster peace: now with express delivery.
stories.vc: Any deal would ease oil prices quickly, a relief for importers like India.

stories.headline: Germany's biggest union launches strikes at Audi and Mercedes
body: IG Metall launched strikes in a wage dispute covering 3.7 million metal and electrical workers.
Audi, Mercedes-Benz and Tata Steel were among those hit.
The union wants a 5% pay rise.
stories.vc: Wage pressure in Germany's car industry adds costs just as it fights Chinese EV competition.

stories.statLabel: US oil profits in six months
stories.headline: US oil firms made $130 billion during the Iran war
body: 51 big US oil and gas companies earned over $130 billion from April to September, the New York Times estimates.
That compares with under $47 billion in the same period last year.
Consumers worldwide are paying much higher prices.
stories.vc: War windfalls flow to producers while importers like India pay more, widening trade gaps.

stories.headline: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman
body: China's foreign minister met a senior Iranian security official and urged dialogue.
Xi Jinping hosted Oman's sultan, the first such visit since 1978.
Beijing is also sending an envoy to the Gulf.
stories.vc: China's growing role as a Gulf mediator matters for oil supply routes it shares with India.

stories.headline: Hungary will name its communist-era informants
body: Hungary's new government will reveal the names of tens of thousands of communist-era informants on Wednesday.
From 1945 to 1989, the secret police used them to spy on neighbours, friends and family.
The goal is to confront the past and rebuild trust.
stories.vc: Transparency moves can improve institutional trust, which investors watch in post-communist states.

stories.headline: Briton Karl Bushby finishes a 28-year walk around the world
body: Karl Bushby, 57, arrived home in Hull after walking about 50,000 km over 28 years.
He crossed jungles, frozen seas and many borders on his 'Goliath Expedition'.
His mother greeted him under a 'Welcome Home Son' banner.
stories.joke: 'Sorry to keep you waiting.' Understatement of the century.
stories.vc: Epic adventure stories like this become books, films and sponsorship gold.

stories.headline: Namma Metro's Pink Line may open on 13 November
body: MP Tejasvi Surya hinted the elevated Pink Line will open on 13 November.
BMRCL says it hasn't yet heard from the PM's office.
The elevated stretch is 7.5 km long with six stations.
stories.joke: The Pink Line: arriving soon™, now with a likely date.
stories.vc: Each new metro line lifts nearby property and retail demand.

stories.headline: Kannada group asks IT firms for local hiring data, despite CM's appeal
body: Karnataka Rakshana Vedike began a month-long drive asking IT and biotech firms for data on jobs given to Kannadigas.
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar had urged groups not to visit IT companies.
Members are handing letters to company heads across the state.
stories.vc: Local-hiring pressure is a new risk factor for tech firms deciding where to expand in India.

stories.headline: MobiKwik swings to profit as costs fall
body: MobiKwik made ₹11.8 crore in the September quarter, against a ₹28.6 crore loss a year ago.
Revenue rose 9.4%.
Lower payment processing and lending costs helped.
stories.joke: A profitable MobiKwik. Wallets everywhere are surprised.
stories.vc: Listed fintechs turning profitable support valuations for private peers.

stories.headline: Clinics On Cloud raises ₹120 crore for its 'health ATMs'
body: Clinics On Cloud raised ₹120 crore at a ₹600 crore valuation from UAE-based Model42.
It makes health ATMs, box clinics and mobile medical units for check-ups and teleconsults.
It will use the UAE as a base to expand to Africa, the US and Southeast Asia.
stories.joke: Check-up at the ATM: insert finger, receive results.
stories.vc: Low-cost health kiosks can reach places hospitals can't, a big market across emerging economies.

stories.headline: Pixxel founder says it stays Indian-owned after US move
body: Pixxel's Awais Ahmed dismissed online questions about the startup's Indian ownership after it set up a US arm.
He says Indian defence and space work stays under the Indian entity.
Rival GalaxEye highlighted its single India-based entity.
stories.vc: Startups selling to both Indian and US governments must carefully ring-fence ownership and data.

stories.headline: Snap settles a teen mental-health lawsuit before trial
body: Snap settled a lawsuit by two teens who said its app fed their depression, anxiety and eating disorders.
They had already settled with Meta, TikTok and YouTube.
It was set to be Snap's first trial in a wave of such cases.
stories.vc: A wave of teen-safety suits is raising legal costs for social apps and shaping product design.
